title: loveholidays reports wider software delivery after putting Codex beyond engineering
friendlyTitle: A travel company lets more staff build software with Codex
summary: In an OpenAI customer case study, travel company loveholidays says AI-assisted code changes rose from 7% to 79% in a year while deployment frequency increased 73% without engineering headcount growth. It built controlled workflows that let product, design and commercial teams prototype and make validated changes.
friendlySummary: loveholidays says teams outside engineering now use Codex inside controlled workflows to test ideas and make some changes. The company reports more frequent deployments without adding engineers.
whyItMatters: The transferable lesson is not simply to hand everyone a coding agent: specialist teams encoded design systems, checks and release practices before broadening access. Businesses considering citizen development should measure successful outcomes and support burden, not just generated code.
friendlyWhyItMatters: AI coding can help more people build, but only when experts add clear rules and tests. Companies should count useful, successful changes—not just more code.
